text:
Marin: quick note from the overnight bring-up for lumen-int6 (new PTQ) against the structured-invoke harness. We're seeing a class of failures where the model emits fragmented JSON with short prose between fragments. Parser marks them as invalid. Failure rate ~2.1%.

Tao: example?

Marin: harness capture: ```
{
  "action": "create_issue",
  "params": {"title": "Payment failure on
```
(then later in the same response) ```
checkout"} 
}
``` Fragmented across emission boundaries.

Sophie: I think I've seen this before—mid-sequence stop/emit behavior. Two quick heuristics: 1) conservative stitcher (concat adjacent fragments up to 2 and parse), 2) fenced-prose-stripper that removes tiny prose lines between brace-bearing fragments. Both risky.

Tao: metrics we care about: parse_pass, semantic_match (action==gold), false_stitch_rate, latency p95, token delta. Also split by context-length.

Marin: prototyped stitcher that only stitches when combined JSON has required keys and no duplicate top-level keys. Local test: failed->0.48%, false_stitch ~0.09%.

Sophie: false-stitchs are scary (they merge distinct actions). Can we add a cheap guard: only stitch if fragments are from the same response and distance < 20 tokens and combined length < 1.5x prompt?

Marin: added those guards. Also added an extra check that param value types match schema (e.g., string vs array). That reduced false_stitch to ~0.04% in small runs.

Tao: propose an AB test: A=baseline, B=conservative-stitch+guards, C=B + immediate retry (temp=0, instruct: "output only JSON") if parse still fails. 12k calls split across context-length.

Sophie: add a tiny decoder-probe: boost brace tokens slightly (1.1x) and penalize common prose tokens like "note", "see" for a 1k run to see if we can reduce fragmentation at the source.

Marin: I'll also add logging of fragment offsets and kvcache length. We need to know if long kv-cache correlates.

lint-bot: scheduled: "lumen-int6-stitch-ab-12k" - queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Tao: sampling: capture up to 250 stitched examples and 250 rejected-fragment examples for manual triage. Sophie, can you help label false-stitchs?

Sophie: yup, I can. Also request adding a flag so we can enable stitcher only for dedicated customers initially.

Marin: timeline: run queued now, results+sample dump+PR proposal by EOD tomorrow. If B or C gets parse_fail <0.4% with false_stitch <0.05% and acceptable latency, we'll propose enabling behind a config flag.

Tao: add token-cost delta to the report for product.

Marin: will do. Thanks everyone. :coffee:
